title: Service echo timeline census: cold vs warm per-stage p50/p95/p99
content:
Summary:
This note collects an exploratory census of end-to-end (E2E) emission timelines for the serving runtime, focusing on p50/p95/p99 decompositions by stage, split by cold vs warm request contexts and by short/medium sequence-length cohorts. The framing here is an attempt to capture the 'service echo' — the internal roundtrip time signature through tokenizer -> serving stages -> emission -> egress — and to highlight where tail risk (p95/p99) concentrates under different operational modes (cold KV miss, large batch contention, and long seqlens).

Goals:
- Produce a compact, reproducible per-stage p50/p95/p99 census for typical API workloads (chat/complete)
- Surface dominant root causes for p99 tails across cold/warm and seqlen cohorts
- Propose experiments and quick mitigations to reduce unit tail cost and outage surface

Data sources and sampling:
- Traces: sampled traces from trace-store (service-traces-prod) for window 2025-02-05 -> 2025-02-11. Sampling targeted endpoints: /v1/generate (text), /v1/chat (chat streaming).
- Cohorts: short (<=64 tokens input), medium (65-512 tokens), long (>512 tokens).
- Context tags: coldstart=true if backend pod reported kv_warm=false on trace; warm otherwise.
- Sampling weight: ensured at least 20k traces per cohort across three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west).

Stage definitions used in decomposition (instrumentation spans):
- tokenize: client decode + server tokenizer (preprocessing)
- kv-lookup: prefix/KV cache lookup + possible remote fetch (cold miss latency included)
- queue-wait: time waiting in batching queue (includes coalescing policy wait)
- model-forward: on-GPU forward passes (includes kernel schedule overhead)
- emit: token emission plumbing, incremental flushes, backpressure stalls
- egress: network egress, response assembly, streaming flush

Aggregate census (selected cohorts, values in ms):
Overall (short cohort, warm): E2E p50=42ms, p95=190ms, p99=760ms
Per-stage breakdown (short/warm):
- tokenize p50=1ms p95=3ms p99=9ms
- kv-lookup p50=2ms p95=8ms p99=25ms
- queue-wait p50=3ms p95=40ms p99=220ms
- model-forward p50=28ms p95=110ms p99=480ms
- emit p50=6ms p95=20ms p99=120ms
- egress p50=2ms p95=5ms p99=10ms

Short cohort, cold (kv miss/cold pod): E2E p50=68ms p95=350ms p99=1600ms
- kv-lookup p50=22ms p95=140ms p99=900ms (remote fetch spikes visible)
- queue-wait p95 increases moderately (p95=70ms) due to KV fetch holding batch locks
- model-forward similar medians but p99 drifts up due to concurrent warmup kernel scheduling

Medium cohort, warm: E2E p50=95ms p95=430ms p99=2200ms
- queue-wait p95=120ms p99=780ms (more batching contention at scale)
- model-forward p95=210ms p99=1100ms

Long cohort (cold): E2E p50=420ms p95=1250ms p99=4300ms
- model-forward dominates tail (p99 ~ 2.5s), but emit p99 also large because of incremental KV misses and bursty client-side chunking

Key observations:
1) Queue-wait is the single most volatile stage across short->medium cohorts: p95/p99 skew primarily driven by batching policy interactions with the KV-fetch path. When a request holds off a batch while waiting on KV, downstream requests pile up and amplify p99.
2) KV-lookup cold misses are catastrophic for p99 even for short seqlens: remote fetches show long-tail network/remote-storage variance. Per-trace heatmap shows a bimodal latency distribution for kv-lookup.
3) Model-forward p99 grows non-linearly with seqlen and with concurrent competing batches on the same GPU (NVLINK/PCIe bus saturation effects).
4) Emit stage has microburst stalls correlated with small-client streamed chunks: a few traces show repeated 50-150ms stalls between token groups, likely due to our backpressure threshold and socket flush policy.
5) Egress is negligible in median but can contribute to p99 in pathological multi-chunk streaming cases (client stalls + server flush granularity).

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Primary tail source for short/medium p99: KV cold misses + locking semantics that block batch head, amplifying queue-wait for followers.
B) For long sequences p99: GPU forward kernel schedule + memory pressure (KV cache misses in-GPU for kv-augmented models) leading to long model-forward tail.
C) Minor but addressable: emit flush policy and small-chunk client patterns cause repeated small waits that add up to p99 inflation.

Quick experiments to validate and mitigate (low effort -> higher):
1) Shadow-route KV cold-miss paths to a separate pool (experimental) to avoid head-of-batch blocking. Measure E2E p95/p99 delta (JIRA-8492).
2) Adjust batching cutoff to max-wait 10ms (from 25ms) for short cohort to reduce queue accumulation. Run A/B on traffic-sampled pods.
3) Add token-level early-emit heuristics for streams: emit partial frame at N tokens or X ms whichever first (tune flush granularity).
4) Pin warmup kernels on cold pod startup to ensure model-forward kernel JIT/compilation is prepopulated (use prewarm daemon).
5) Introduce a KV fetch fallback: if remote fetch > 80ms, return an approximate/empty prefix and mark trace for downstream quality check (trade-off must be validated).

Repro commands / quick instrumentation checks:
- Query trace store for top p99 traces: curl -H 'X-Auth:...' https://trace-store/api/search?q=service:runtime AND endpoint:/v1/generate AND percentile:99 cohort:short --limit 500
- Extract per-stage times with trace-slicer tool: trace-slicer --trace-ids $(cat top99.txt) --stages tokenize,kv-lookup,queue-wait,model-forward,emit,egress --out csv
- Local microbenchmark to reproduce kv cold miss: scripts/kv_cold_miss_driver.py --seqlen 32 --repeats 1000 --parallel 16 --target-pool=prod-sim

Risk/notes:
- Any change to batching policy affects throughput/cost. Lower max-wait reduces p99 but may increase cost (more batches -> lower packing). Need econ model to estimate unit cost delta.
- Shadow routing or separate pools adds management overhead and possible cold-start cost elsewhere.
- Emit heuristics require careful correctness checks for streaming semantics and partial JSON responses.

Next steps (owner + timeline):
- 1 week: Run experiment (1) shadow-route KV misses to separate pool on canary (owner: Benji). Collect 7d p50/p95/p99.
- 2 weeks: Tune batching max-wait for short cohort on ~10% traffic, measure throughput and unit cost (owner: Aisha).
- 3 weeks: Prototype early emit flush policy in sandbox and run end-to-end regression tests with chat clients (owner: Lina).

Meeting notes / sync:
- Quick sync scheduled 2025-02-21 15:00 PST with eng-serving-runtime, infra, and metrics. Agenda: show top tail traces, decide on canary config for shadow routing, and evaluate cost model.

Appendix: interesting trace signatures to hand off (trace-ids): trace-20250207-4312, trace-20250208-9981, trace-20250209-1127.

Open questions:
- Acceptable unit-cost delta for batching change? (need product input)
- Do we prefer approximate prefix fallback over delayed exactness for KV cold misses?

Owner note: this is exploratory and intentionally rough. Primary goal is to converge on 2 quick experiments to validate hypotheses A and C.
